sources.author: Sarah Chen
sources.headline: Staff Engineer @ Anthropic | Previously Google DeepMind | Building reliable AI systems
sources.post_summary: Just shipped a breakdown of how we think about agent reliability at scale. The dirty secret: 80% of agent failures aren't model failures — they're tool call failures, context window mismanagement, and bad retry logic. Most teams are optimizing the wrong layer. Here's what actually moves the needle.

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Founder @ Stackwise | YC W25 | Ex-Stripe | Making infra boring again
sources.post_summary: We crossed $1M ARR this week. 11 months, 3 engineers, zero enterprise sales team. The entire motion was Claude Code + a Slack channel. I'll tell you what surprised me: the bottleneck was never the AI — it was the humans who couldn't review output fast enough. Sharing the exact workflow we use to ship 10x faster without losing quality.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Head of Platform Engineering @ Databricks | Distributed systems nerd | Speaker
sources.post_summary: Hot take: MCP is the API design pattern that finally solves tool integration for agents — but 90% of implementations get the auth model wrong and ship context leaks. Spent the last two weeks auditing 12 production MCP servers. The failure modes are consistent and fixable. Thread below.

sources.author: Jordan Okafor
sources.headline: GTM Engineer | AI-native revenue ops | Building the RevOps stack of 2027
sources.post_summary: Everyone is talking about AI SDRs. Nobody is talking about what happens after the meeting books. The real leverage is in the handoff: structured context from the agent to the AE, pre-researched in real time, synced to CRM before the call starts. We 3x'd AE close rate in 60 days by fixing the handoff, not the top of funnel.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | Revenue Intelligence | GTM Strategy
sources.post_summary: AI SDRs are not replacing human SDRs. They're replacing the 4 hours a day humans waste on research, sequencing, and CRM hygiene. The teams winning right now aren't cutting headcount — they're redirecting it. One rep doing strategic work beats three doing mechanical work every time.

sources.author: Tamara Boyce
sources.headline: RevOps Lead @ Series B SaaS | HubSpot → Salesforce migrations | Pipeline analytics
sources.post_summary: We killed our 14-step outbound sequence last quarter. Replaced it with a 3-touch sequence with a real personalization signal in step 1. Reply rate went from 1.8% to 6.3%. The lesson: most sequences are long because nobody wants to make the hard decision about what actually matters.

sources.author: Marcus Edgerton
sources.headline: GTM Engineer | Clay + Apollo + AI | Building revenue infrastructure for B2B startups
sources.post_summary: Most GTM engineers are just power users of Clay. Real GTM engineering is owning the data pipeline end to end — enrichment logic, routing rules, scoring models, CRM hygiene automation, and alerting when something breaks. Took me 18 months to learn the difference. Now I charge accordingly.

sources.author: Priya Nath
sources.headline: VP of Marketing | B2B Content Strategy | Demand Gen | ex-Gong, ex-Drift
sources.post_summary: Dark social is not a strategy. Posting consistently on LinkedIn IS a strategy — and it compounds. We traced 31% of inbound demos last quarter back to a LinkedIn post from 60+ days prior. The content your buyers read before they ever fill out a form is doing more work than your paid ads. Invest accordingly.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Quit my FAANG job to build in public | 0 → $8k MRR in 90 days | Founder @ Loopkit
sources.post_summary: Priya shares a raw breakdown of her first 90 days after leaving Google — including the month she made $0, the cold DM that landed her first 10 customers, and the exact pricing mistake that cost her $2k in revenue. Ends with: 'nobody talks about the weeks before the screenshot.'

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Self-taught dev → shipped 3 products | Writing about the unglamorous parts of building solo
sources.post_summary: Marcus posts a simple before/after: 18 months ago he was copying Stack Overflow answers and didn't understand what an API was. Today he just crossed $1k MRR on a tool he built in a weekend. The post is mostly about what changed — not the code skills, but the willingness to ship ugly v1s without apologizing.

sources.author: Tomas Eriksson
sources.headline: Building AI tools for small businesses | ex-agency founder | shipping weekly
sources.post_summary: Tomas shares that he spent 3 weeks building an AI feature nobody asked for, then added a dead-simple CSV export in 2 hours and got 40 upgrade requests the same day. The lesson he draws: 'I keep optimizing for impressive. My users keep asking for boring.' Thread format with real Stripe screenshots.

sources.author: Danielle Osei
sources.headline: Teacher → Software Engineer in 14 months | Now building EdTech solo | Career changer helping career changers
sources.post_summary: Danielle posts about the moment she realized her bootcamp job hunt strategy was wrong — she was applying to 20 jobs a day and getting nothing, then landed 3 offers in 3 weeks after switching to building one small public project and writing about it. Post breaks down the exact project, the exact posts, and the exact emails she sent. Comments flooded with other career-pivoters asking for the template.
